title: Taipei Leads Asia with Millions of Bike Rentals

image.attribution: GeorgeLouis at English Wikipedia / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-SA-3.0

main_content:
Taipei has emerged as a role model for Asian cities, with a public bike rental program that has reached 20 million trips per year because of low rates and an abundance of bikes throughout the crowded Taiwanese capital.

Envoys from Tokyo and Singapore, two other dense Asian cities, have visited Taipei to ask the city’s transportation department how the rental program, known as YouBike, has developed.

Interest surged after the seven-year-old program suddenly saw rentals double from 2013 to 2014. Biking took off in Taipei because more than 30 percent of people already commute by metro or bus. They willingly pedal the final kilometer to work if rentals are close to their final metro or bus stop. Taipei’s city government has placed many of its 222 rental kiosks in exactly those locations.

“Taipei’s population density is high and people’s usage of buses and the metro has reached a certain level,” said Liu Chia-yu, a division chief under the city government’s transportation department. “Those people actually can use YouBike in the natural course of their movements.”

Taipei now lacks the traffic jams that are notorious in Asian cities such as Bangkok, Beijing and Jakarta. Air pollution is also less severe in here.

Taiwan-based Giant Manufacturing, a maker of bikes that are sold internationally, operates the YouBike system and supplies it with 7,200 clean, orange bikes.

Chang Da-you, a 28-year-old office worker in Taipei, is a typical YouBike commuter. He rides five kilometers to and from work every day that it’s not raining. On weekends, he bicycles up to 20 kilometers along a river trail.

“It’s convenient. Wherever you go, there it is,” Chang said. “If there’s a metro stop nearby there’s also YouBike, so you can take the metro to your bike and ride the bike to any other place.”

questions.question: Why is the public bike rental program in Taipei so successful?
options: It operates only on weekends when public transport is less reliable.
It has convenient kiosks located near metro and bus stops for last-mile travel.
It offers a wide variety of bike models to choose from.
It is heavily subsidized by the government to reduce traffic congestion.
questions.answer: It has convenient kiosks located near metro and bus stops for last-mile travel.

questions.question: What does the article say about the share of people in Taipei who commute by metro or bus?
options: More than 30 percent of people commute by metro or bus.
About 30 percent of people commute by metro or bus.
Less than 25 percent of people commute by metro or bus.
About 75 percent of people commute by metro or bus.
questions.answer: More than 30 percent of people commute by metro or bus.

questions.question: What are two good consequences of the bike rental program mentioned in the article?
options: It has caused more traffic jams and worse air pollution.
It has led to fewer traffic jams and less severe air pollution.
It has reduced the number of buses in operation and increased pedestrian traffic.
It has increased car ownership and made roads wider.
questions.answer: It has led to fewer traffic jams and less severe air pollution.
